title: A Two-level SLC Cache Hierarchy for Hybrid SSDs
problem: Triple-level-cell (TLC) NAND flash memory suffers lower write performance and endurance compared to single-level-cell (SLC); hybrid SLC-TLC SSDs use SLC as write cache but existing cache management schemes do not effectively optimize granularity and cold/hot data separation.
motivation: TLC dominates high-density NAND production but write performance bottleneck; hybrid SLC-TLC architectures are commercially ubiquitous yet cache optimization remains inadequate.
method: Proposes two-level SLC cache hierarchy (L1 and L2) with varying data granularity (coarse L2, fine L1). Implements dynamic segmentation of L1 and L2 cache capacity based on write size characteristics of running applications. Evaluates against existing SLC cache schemes.
key_novelty: Hierarchical two-level SLC cache with dynamic granularity management and application-aware cache partitioning for SLC-TLC hybrid SSDs.
contributions: Two-level SLC cache hierarchy design with fine and coarse granularity tiers
Dynamic cache segmentation strategy based on workload write patterns
12.6%-25.1% I/O performance improvement over existing hybrid SSD cache schemes
baselines: existing SLC cache management schemes for hybrid SSD
limitations: Energy efficiency and flash endurance impact not characterized; generalization to emerging 3D NAND architectures not discussed.
primary_theme: hierarchical SLC cache for hybrid SSD performance
